about: Tiny Little Office signatures (src/kit/sign.ts, src/kit/envelope.ts, docs/crypto/signing.md). The signed bytes are the UTF-8 of: 'tinyoffice' LF app LF created LF body NUL title NUL by, where created is whole minutes since 2020-01-01T00:00Z in base 36 (empty when the document has none). Ed25519 signs them as they are (RFC 8032, deterministic); ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256 is the fallback, its signature r|s, 64 bytes, and different every time, so its vector is checked by verifying. A public key travels as base64url without padding of its raw form: 32 bytes for Ed25519, 65 (0x04|x|y) for P-256, which is how a verifier tells them apart. The fingerprint is the first 5 bytes of SHA-256(raw public key) in hex, a hyphen after the fifth character. The envelope's document is the Ed25519 vector as a Word Processor document carries it: the message is read from it by taking title, by, created, key and sig out of its head. These keys are published test keys: never sign with them.
